panels.title: AUC per round — IID baseline
panels.description: AUC reported by the server each round for the IID partition. E1 records only final metrics per fold, so E2 is the run that carries a round-by-round curve. Rendered as a bar chart over the round number: `round` is an integer, not a timestamp, so a time-series panel would place every point in 1970 and report "Data outside time range".

targets.rawSql: SELECT round, auc, run FROM e1_convergence WHERE run = 'iid' ORDER BY round

panels.title: AUC per round — non-IID partitions
panels.description: Same metric across IID and the two Dirichlet skews, so the cost of non-IID is visible round by round. Rendered as a bar chart over the round number: `round` is an integer, not a timestamp, so a time-series panel would place every point in 1970 and report "Data outside time range".

targets.rawSql: SELECT round, auc, run FROM e1_convergence WHERE run <> 'iid' ORDER BY round

panels.title: Per-client AUC — FedAvg vs FedProx
panels.description: Each bar is one silo. A model that is good on average but poor on the smallest silo is not deployable, so the spread matters more than the mean.

targets.rawSql: SELECT label, strategy, value FROM e5_fairness WHERE view = 'client' ORDER BY label

panels.title: Recall by churn reason
panels.description: Share of churners flagged by the global top-10% cut-off, per reason. Churn Category is only populated for customers who churned, so AUC is undefined here and recall is the meaningful metric.

targets.rawSql: SELECT label, strategy, value FROM e5_fairness WHERE view = 'reason' ORDER BY label

panels.title: Privacy-utility curve (E4)
panels.description: AUC against epsilon. The non-DP row has epsilon = 0 in the table because the accountant reports nothing; read it as infinite budget.

targets.rawSql: SELECT noise_multiplier, epsilon, auc, pr_auc FROM e4_privacy ORDER BY noise_multiplier
